name: Ishvi
overview: Ishvi was a male member of the tribe of Asher, identified specifically as a son of Asher. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, linking him to the early patriarchal narratives and the formation of the Israelite tribes. His inclusion in the tribal lists underscores his place within the covenant community of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Ishvi appears in Scripture without an explicit meaning provided. It is a proper name recorded in Genesis 46:17, and there is no indication that it was given directly by God or that it carries a special title.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ishvi as a son of Asher, situating him within the family lineage of one of Jacob's twelve sons. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ishvi's significance lies in his role as a progenitor within the tribe of Asher, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. His mention among those who went to Egypt marks him as part of the foundational generation that experienced the migration leading to Israel's sojourn in Egypt. Additionally, the later reference to the Ishvites in Numbers 26:44 indicates the ongoing recognition of his descendants within the tribal structure of Israel.
